I don't know if South Africa meets the bar of genocide yet, but it is certainly heading that way. 1. comments.text:
Something that should've been mentioned is the one of Chase's five C's: Context

Zelenskyj had always been very respectful towards Trump since even before the election. During that time Trump, on the other hand, stated time and time again that basically ALL support Biden gave Ukraine was foolish and wrong and should never have happened. And for the last week or so leading up to this meeting, Trump had (among other things)
1) Called Zelenskyj a dictator
2) Said Ukraine started the war
3) Invited Russia to a meeting and not Ukraine
4) Publically stated Ukraine can't have their missing land back and can't join Nato ever (and some similar statements severely weakening Ukraines bargaining position before talks even had begun)

If you put that into consideration you might have more understanding for why Zelenskyj was triggered by Vance saying it's time for diplomacy. Not only had diplomacy with Putin failed before, the diplomacy option was at it's all-time-low for Ukraine at this point, thanks to the Trump regime.

Could Zelenskyj have handled things differently? For sure. And he should have. But the Trump regime had been picking a fight with him for quite a while, AND made damn sure to  weaken Ukraine's position in favor of Russia. I say they wanted this fight.

I mean, come on, think about it. A temporary peace deal would benefit Russia far more than Ukraine. Russia is struggling now, but given time, they will rebuild their military much faster than Ukraine, which will be focused on reconstruction. That means Ukraine would come out weaker, while Russia regains its strength and prepares for another invasion.

If Ukraine gives up territory, they lose strategic depth, resources, and defensive positions, while Russia gains all of that. This war cannot end until Russia is left incapable of attacking Ukraine again. Otherwise, stopping now just makes Ukraine smaller and weaker while making Russia bigger and stronger, setting the stage for an even worse war down the line.

People pushing for a rushed “peace” don’t understand history, strategy, or even basic geopolitics. If you think this is about ‘compassion’ or ‘realism,’ you’re missing the point—you’re just enabling future aggression.

replies.author: @shepherdwarrior777
replies.text:
Today, we witnessed Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau’s address to the nation regarding the imposition of U.S. tariff restrictions on Canadian goods entering the American market. Trudeau labeled this a "trade war" and called upon Canadians to unite as a single political nation in opposition. However, he opened his speech by equating Trump’s America with Putin’s Russia—an ideological trap that distorts the true nature of the conflict. If we extend the metaphor, Trudeau plays the role of the goat leading the flock to slaughter. A harsh analogy? Perhaps. But an accurate one. Why?

       The roots of this conflict stretch back to the founding of the United States itself. America was established as a new civilizational project, distinct from the entrenched colonial, political, and religious structures of Europe. While Canada remained, in essence, a British colony — eventually morphing into a globalist, liberal-democratic project governed by transnational corporate interests — the United States was built upon land, tradition, and the Christian ideal. Trump’s America, encapsulated in the slogan "Make America Great Again" (MAGA), is a return to these foundational principles. Let us call this vision "Trumpism."

       Trumpism’s proposal to Canada — that it should become the 51st U.S. state — is not merely an economic or political move but a call for liberation from its status as a colony of globalist transnational elites. The true power behind Trudeau is not the Canadian people but the aristocratic and royal families of Europe, with the Vatican at their helm — the very forces from which the American founders sought to escape in the 18th century (1776). The language may have changed, but the core power structure remains.

       Why did Trudeau begin his speech by tying America’s nationalist economic policies to Russia? The answer is simple: Russia, too, is a nation built upon land and tradition. After the collapse of the Soviet Union, it fell under the influence of globalist liberal-democratic ideology, which promoted the extraction of national resources for the benefit of "world markets" at the expense of the homeland. Does this sound familiar? Before Trump, America followed the same path — draining its wealth, engaging in endless foreign wars, and subordinating its infrastructure and financial system to global markets that exploited the hard work of ordinary Americans.

       The elite factions backing Trudeau are not Canadian nationalists (Rooted people); their true allegiance lies in London and the British Crown, to whom they swear fealty. Have you ever heard the phrase "We, the Canadian people" in an oath of citizenship? No, and you never will — unless Canada embraces a true national identity, which, allegorically, is what Trump’s vision of the 51st state represents.

       Historically, Catherine the Great’s Russian Empire, the later Tsars, and even Bolshevik Russia supported the land-rooted America of Jefferson and Lincoln, recognizing in it a natural ally. In contrast, Britain — the queen of the seas and the mother of transnational piracy — has never been a nation of land and tradition but of maritime dominance and global financial manipulation. The essence of the current tariff war between Canada, Mexico, and Trump’s nationalist (People of the land) America is thus not merely economic but revolutionary. As citizens of these opposing projects, we must decide where we stand: on solid ground or adrift in the Atlantic and Pacific oceans, subject to the whims of transnational elites.

       As Thomas Jefferson famously warned, "Merchants have no country. The mere spot they stand on does not constitute so strong an attachment as that from which they draw their gains." These words resonate now more than ever, as Canada’s ruling elites prioritize transnational interests over the well-being of their own people. The choice ahead is clear: either reclaim national sovereignty or remain servants to a global order indifferent to the fate of ordinary citizens.

....This message comes from a Swedish psychologist, P. Wirsén. I couldn't resist sharing his words about the meeting between Zelensky and Trump. It is very important to understand this. So, read this: "It became painfully clear what narcissistic power games and psychopathology look like when Trump openly humiliated Zelensky at the White House. In front of recognized journalists from around the world, he called Zelensky "disrespectful," questioned his loyalty, and insinuated that he did not deserve support from the United States. As if that were not enough, he warned that Zelensky could cause a third world war—a classic psychopathic trait where threats are used as a means to gain control.

It was not just a sign of poor diplomacy; it was a demonstrative manifestation of power, marked by narcissism and psychopathy.

🔹 Grandiose self-image and need for submission
— Trump expected Zelensky to show gratitude and admiration. When that did not happen, he publicly punished him. People with narcissistic personality disorder cannot tolerate their self-image being questioned and use humiliation as a defense.

🔹Manipulation and threats
— Blaming someone for a potential disaster is a classic psychopathic tactic. By saying that Zelensky is "playing with World War III," he shifts the blame onto him while portraying himself as the only one who can prevent the catastrophe.

🔹 Impulsive and emotionally driven exertion of power
— When Trump felt challenged by Zelensky, he abruptly ended the meeting. A stable and strategic leader would have handled the situation diplomatically, but someone with psychopathic traits instinctively reacts based on their sense of losing control.

But why did he do this in front of the press? This is why narcissists and psychopaths love to display their power publicly. By humiliating Zelensky before the eyes of the world, he not only sends a message to him but to all leaders and nations: "I am the one who decides, and those who disobey will be crushed."

What we witnessed was not just a president behaving inappropriately. It was a textbook example of how narcissistic and psychopathic leaders use humiliation, threats, and manipulation to assert their power. And just like in destructive relationships, this is never about building but about controlling.

And why was the agreement about minerals? What is needed to drive a Tesla? Narcissists, dictators, and psychopaths idealize each other and scratch each other's backs in unholy alliances.

Trump can no longer claim to be the leader of the free world. His actions today do not place him among democratic statesmen but among the dictators of history. A true leader builds alliances through respect and diplomacy, while a dictator rules through threats, fear, and humiliation. replies.text:
The subject of john oliver, jon stewart and the daily show (for this comments sake... let us call it all of the leftist "comedy" talk shows) came up when a colleague (fellow psychologist) and I were discussing politics a few months ago. Although we were both in agreement regarding the general shitlib inanity of the HBO show, my friend was surprised when I explained that the real insidiousness of it is its unmistakably hypnotic structure and pacing.
l ended up pulling up an episode or two off of youtube to show her what I meant. All of the segments I've ever seen from this show follow the same repetitive format: present some "argumentation" and "facts" for about 10 seconds, then quickly follow these up with a snarky quip (which themselves overwhelmingly take the form of complete
non-sequitur or otherwise absurd metaphor) before any rational processing of the preceding argument can take place in the mind of the viewer. Further telling is that the only 'beats' or mental pauses in the show's pacing exist solely to highlight the approving laughter or applause of the studio audience. Repeat this basic formula without variation20-40 times in a row and you have one of the 12-20 minute'segments' that form the backbone of the show.
The end effect is (obviously) not to deliver information, but rather to literally teach the viewers -- on a subconscious level -- to mentally associate derisive laughter with any person or opinion that is at odds with the narrative's take on the chosen issue. And it accomplishes this by maintaining a strict adherence to a roughly 20-second cycle in which a stimulus is presented, and a response is cued. This is the sense in which the show is fundamentally hypnotic in effect -- even moreso than its precursors in the genre (Daily Show,Colbert,etc).
To my mind, oliver's show is representative of the media's increasing mastery of the methodologies of mass conditioning; in fact it is almost such a perfect technical accomplishment that I would almost have to admire it on technical grounds, which moreover is in the hands of the entirely wrong people.

We sometimes use that word to describe ourselves because American culture is so ingrained in our society, for better and for worse. I've personally always felt that connection across the Atlantic, despite having never been to America. But the US with Trump at the helm has chosen to sever our connection. It can be repaired in the future, maybe, but for now, it's over. And I'm honestly heartbroken by it.

comments.text:
Former President of Poland Lech Walesa wrote the following letter to Trump.

Your Excellency, Mr. President,

We watched the report of your conversation with the President of Ukraine, Volodymyr Zelensky, with fear and distaste. We find it insulting that you expect Ukraine to show respect and gratitude for the material assistance provided by the United States in its fight against Russia. Gratitude is owed to the heroic Ukrainian soldiers who shed their blood in defense of the values of the free world. They have been dying on the front lines for more than 11 years in the name of these values and the independence of their homeland, which was attacked by Putin’s Russia.

We do not understand how the leader of a country that symbolizes the free world cannot recognize this.

Our alarm was also heightened by the atmosphere in the Oval Office during this conversation, which reminded us of the interrogations we endured at the hands of the Security Services and the debates in Communist courts. Prosecutors and judges, acting on behalf of the all-powerful communist political police, would explain to us that they held all the power while we held none. They demanded that we cease our activities, arguing that thousands of innocent people suffered because of us. They stripped us of our freedoms and civil rights because we refused to cooperate with the government or express gratitude for our oppression. We are shocked that President Volodymyr Zelensky was treated in the same manner.

The history of the 20th century shows that whenever the United States sought to distance itself from democratic values and its European allies, it ultimately became a threat to itself. President Woodrow Wilson understood this when he decided in 1917 that the United States must join World War I. President Franklin Delano Roosevelt understood this when, after the attack on Pearl Harbor in December 1941, he resolved that the war to defend America must be fought not only in the Pacific but also in Europe, in alliance with the nations under attack by the Third Reich.

We remember that without President Ronald Reagan and America’s financial commitment, the collapse of the Soviet empire would not have been possible. President Reagan recognized that millions of enslaved people suffered in Soviet Russia and the countries it had subjugated, including thousands of political prisoners who paid for their defense of democratic values with their freedom. His greatness lay, among other things, in his unwavering decision to call the USSR an “Empire of Evil” and to fight it decisively. We won, and today, the statue of President Ronald Reagan stands in Warsaw, facing the U.S. Embassy.

Mr. President, material aid—military and financial—can never be equated with the blood shed in the name of Ukraine’s independence and the freedom of Europe and the entire free world. Human life is priceless; its value cannot be measured in money. Gratitude is due to those who sacrifice their blood and their freedom. This is self-evident to us, the people of Solidarity, former political prisoners of the communist regime under Soviet Russia.

We call on the United States to uphold the guarantees made alongside Great Britain in the 1994 Budapest Memorandum, which established a direct obligation to defend Ukraine’s territorial integrity in exchange for its relinquishment of nuclear weapons. These guarantees are unconditional—there is no mention of treating such assistance as an economic transaction.

Signed,

Lech Wałęsa, former political prisoner, President of Poland

 As a Norwegian, I am with you all the way Canada! Americans, you also got my support! And Ukraine, you will get through this. You are the strongest people on Earth. It will be painful, but you will have your freedom and your honor intact!

comments.text:
Former President of Poland Lech Walesa wrote the following letter to Trump.
Your Excellency, Mr. President,
We watched the report of your conversation with the President of Ukraine, Volodymyr Zelensky, with fear and distaste. We find it insulting that you expect Ukraine to show respect and gratitude for the material assistance provided by the United States in its fight against russia. Gratitude is owed to the heroic Ukrainian soldiers who shed their blood in defense of the values of the free world. They have been dying on the front lines for more than 11 years in the name of these values and the independence of their homeland, which was attacked by Putin’s russia.
We do not understand how the leader of a country that symbolizes the free world cannot recognize this.
Our alarm was also heightened by the atmosphere in the Oval Office during this conversation, which reminded us of the interrogations we endured at the hands of the Security Services and the debates in Communist courts. Prosecutors and judges, acting on behalf of the all-powerful communist political police, would explain to us that they held all the power while we held none. They demanded that we cease our activities, arguing that thousands of innocent people suffered because of us. They stripped us of our freedoms and civil rights because we refused to cooperate with the government or express gratitude for our oppression. We are shocked that President Volodymyr Zelensky was treated in the same manner.
The history of the 20th century shows that whenever the United States sought to distance itself from democratic values and its European allies, it ultimately became a threat to itself. President Woodrow Wilson understood this when he decided in 1917 that the United States must join World War I. President Franklin Delano Roosevelt understood this when, after the attack on Pearl Harbor in December 1941, he resolved that the war to defend America must be fought not only in the Pacific but also in Europe, in alliance with the nations under attack by the Third Reich.
We remember that without President Ronald Reagan and America’s financial commitment, the collapse of the Soviet empire would not have been possible. President Reagan recognized that millions of enslaved people suffered in Soviet russia and the countries it had subjugated, including thousands of political prisoners who paid for their defense of democratic values with their freedom. His greatness lay, among other things, in his unwavering decision to call the USSR an “Empire of Evil” and to fight it decisively. We won, and today, the statue of President Ronald Reagan stands in Warsaw, facing the U.S. Embassy.
Mr. President, material aid—military and financial—can never be equated with the blood shed in the name of Ukraine’s independence and the freedom of Europe and the entire free world. Human life is priceless; its value cannot be measured in money. Gratitude is due to those who sacrifice their blood and their freedom. This is self-evident to us, the people of Solidarity, former political prisoners of the communist regime under Soviet russia.
We call on the United States to uphold the guarantees made alongside Great Britain in the 1994 Budapest Memorandum, which established a direct obligation to defend Ukraine’s territorial integrity in exchange for its relinquishment of nuclear weapons. These guarantees are unconditional—there is no mention of treating such assistance as an economic transaction.
Signed,
Lech Wałęsa, former political prisoner, President of Poland

En Martinique et dans les autres départements d'outre mer ce sont les békés (les anciennes familles de colons français qui autrefois ordonnées le commerce d'esclaves) qui contrôlent la majeure partie de l'alimentaire importée, il fixent des prix bien supérieurs aux coûts de transports pour engranger des marges plus importantes. L'Etat, plutôt que d'imposer aux békés de baisser leurs prix avec par exemple un contrôle du coût du transport et l'obligation d'aligner leur prix aux prix de la métropole en incluant le coût calculé du transport, choisis de supprimer la TVA, ce qui fera des recettes en moins dans le budget de l'Etat, ils pourront ensuite imposer le discours qui dit qu'il y a trop de dépense pour un plus casser l'Etat redistributif français.

Pour résumer nous payons tous pour que les békés et d'autres industriels s'enrichissent sur le dos des martiniquais et à présent de l'ensemble de français de métropoles ou d'outre mer . Ce qu'il se passe c'est un détournement de l'argent public qui finit directement dans les poches de quelques privilégiés pendant que l'hôpital, l'éducation nationale et tous les services publics tombent en miettes. Il y'a de nombreux exemples comme celui ci, c'est un cas d'école des politiques néo-libérales telle que celle de Macron. Là ils suppriment la TVA, demain ils baisseront le remboursement des médicaments parce que vous comprenez il faut faire des économies sinon la dette augmente... Il n'y a pas plus ou moins d'argent. Ils choisissent juste de distribuer l'argent de nos impôts aux responsables des problèmes ou de faire payer les citoyens pour les marges anormales de certains plutôt que de leur demander de rogner sur leurs marges. Toutes les françaises et les français sont perdants, sauf eux. Prenez en conscience, encore une fois c'est loin d'être le seul sujet sur lequel cette méthode est appliquée.

Ho 16 anni alle spalle di comunicazione giornaliera in inglese con persone di tutte le nazionalità in ambito di programmazione e videogiochi, sia personale che lavorativo.

comments.text: Ascoltare l’intera conversazione aiuta a comprendere il contesto molto meglio rispetto a frammenti isolati. Trump ha dichiarato chiaramente di voler fare da mediatore per un accordo di pace, con l’obiettivo di interrompere una guerra che non sarebbe mai dovuta iniziare. Forse Zelenskyy avrebbe potuto fermarsi a un certo punto della conversazione, quando il dialogo stava ancora procedendo bene, evitando di insistere su quanto la Russia abbia rispettato o meno gli accordi passati e di definire Putin un ‘assassino’. Diciamo che probabilmente non era il momento giusto per portare la discussione su certi binari, quasi costringendo Trump a dichiarare apertamente che, in qualità di mediatore, non può accettare un certo tipo di linguaggio, per poi un attimo dopo chiamare Putin e cercare un accordo, quando fino a poco prima lo si era attaccato pesantemente in mondovisione. I fatti sono noti e ciascuno può farsi la propria opinione. Zelenskyy, senza mettere sul piatto argomenti di disprezzo verso la controparte russa, avrebbe anche potuto ad un certo punto ritirarsi in privato con Trump per discutere una tregua: se avesse davvero avuto l’intenzione di mettere fine alla guerra, almeno per curiosità, avrebbe potuto ascoltare le condizioni di Trump, con la totale libertà di rifiutarle

Trump nel suo essere ermetico ma pragmatico, ha detto chiaramente alcuni aspetti importanti: 1) Ha reso onore al coraggio e alle capacità degli ucraini; 2) Ha detto che troppi soldi sono stati spesi per una guerra che non sembra vedere la fine dopo 3 anni; 3) l'accordo con gli USA per l'estrazione delle terre rare, lascia intendere che porterà i privati USA sul suolo ucraino, fungendo da deterrente per Putin (in genere queste operazioni portano sui territori milizie private a tutela dell'investimento).

Poteva essere reso meglio anche la ragione del diverbio tra Vance e Zelensky, che ha dato origine a tutto: Zelensky chiede frontalmente al vice presidente, che tipo di diplomazia stia portando avanti, facendo intendere che lui non la vede.
Questi sono errori non comprensibili in diplomazia internazionale.
Vance si è difeso perchè, giustamente, non può soprassedere ad un attacco frontale davanti alle televisioni mondiali.
Zelensky poteva fare la stessa domanda in privato, dove avrebbe avuto un confronto forse duro, ma che non mirasse ad una umiliazione.

Al di là dell'analisi sulle parole che possono essere interpretate anche diversamente, è un fatto che la Russia non può perdere questa guerra e non la perderà. Piaccia o meno, giusto o sbagliato che sia, serve un compromesso per l'obiettivo superiore che è la pace.

Zelensky ha insistito su garanzie che, tradotte, significano armi, ingresso nella NATO, nell'UE, e costi di ricostruzione a carico della Russia. In pratica la terza guerra mondiale.

Se la Russia perdesse, di fatto si compirebbe il primo passo per la formalizzazione di quest'alleanza, oltre a un probabile effetto domino degli stati "cuscinetto" confinanti.
La dottrina russa sul nucleare è chiara e dichiarata a riguardo, sanno di non poter perdere e il mondo sa che ne farebbero uso se necessario.
Tuttavia, proprio per le impreviste difficoltà che menzioni e perché certamente la Russia non vorrebbe mai ricorrere al nucleare con le implicazioni che avrebbe su scala internazionale, si è aperta una finestra per negoziare, dove entrambi i paesi potrebbero uscirne parzialmente vincitori attraverso un compromesso. Orsini vergognoso vedremo che premio avrà in cambio. 1:21 C’è un aspetto di questo incontro che passerà alla Storia che in pochi stanno considerando. A me che ci lavoro con le lingue e che passo la vita a mediare tra culture mi è parso subito evidente: 

l’inglese di Zelensky è buono, ma non è eccellente. 

Ho guardato tutti e 50 minuti. Fatelo anche voi. Farsi un'idea di come stiano le cose è un dovere, oggi più che mai. 

Trump esordisce così: “è un onore avere qui il Presidente Zelensky, ci conosciamo da molto tempo e abbiamo lavorato bene in passato e continueremo a farlo, apprezziamo il suo lavoro. Abbiamo parlato con Putin e siamo pronti a una negoziazione”. 
Zelensky ricambia, con tono molto sommesso elogia Trump e dice che se riuscirà a fermare Putin, questa cosa dovrebbe essere affissa sulle mura della Casa Bianca. Questo esordio già di per sé preannuncia che Zelensky non crede molto nell’impresa. 

Dopodiché Zelensky comincia a mostrare foto dei prigionieri ucraini per mostrare quanto sia cattivo Putin. 

Trump continua a insistere che lavoreranno per il “cessate il fuoco”, Zelensky continua a dire che sarà impossibile, perché Putin non manterrà la parola.
Trump dice che con lui, invece, Putin manterrà la parola. 

Ora, se io fossi Zelensky, visto che c’è la stampa davanti, e quindi il mondo intero, stringerei la mano di Trump, mi direi fiducioso sul suo operato, saluterei e andrei via. 

Invece no. Purtroppo l’incontro va avanti. 
 
Zelensky dice che anche con Trump, in passato, Putin non ha mantenuto la parola. Che per ben 25 volte, Putin ha firmato accordi che non ha rispettato.

Da qui in poi si peggiora soltanto. Zelensky comincia uno sproloquio infinito di parecchi minuti in un inglese che peggiora sempre di più, accusa Putin di non volere la pace, perché, testualmente “Putin ci odia” e non rispetterà l’accordo con Trump, è una cosa che si può solo sperare. E non rendendosi contro che ha appena dichiarato davanti a tutta la stampa americana che Trump non verrà rispettato, non capendo che quel suo inglese alle orecchie degli americani suona come un grattare sulla lavagna, arriva al delirio affermando che Putin dovrà pagare tutti i danni perché la guerra l’ha cominciata lui.

È finita. La stampa presente comincia a prendere in giro Zelensky. Del perché lo comincino a trattare in quel modo potrei scriverci un trattato di antropologia. Ve lo risparmio dandovi come immagine Christian De Sica che col calzino bucato sale sulla barca dei ricchi. 
Zelensky appare d'improvviso così, come un poveraccio venuto col cappello in mano, che vorrebbe però dire agli americani cosa debbono fare. 

Non è un caso che addirittura gli chiedano perché non si sia degnato di indossare un abito decente. Persino qua, ad onor del vero, Trump lo difende dicendo che a lui piace molto come sta vestito.
 
Zelensky si innervosisce e comincia a perdere la bussola. 
Diventa tutti contro uno. 

Incalzato da vicepresidente Vance, che molto aggressivamente ma a questo punto anche giustamente gli fa presente che si sta provando la diplomazia e che è inutile continuare a dire che Trump non riuscirà, Zelensky risponde con saccenza, chiedendogli se sia mai stato In Ucraina, come a dire “che ne sai tu dei problemi nostri”.

Qui la faccenda diventa personale. Trump sta per perdere la pazienza, Vance a quel punto gli ricorda la partecipazione di Zelensky alla Convention dei democratici durante la campagna elettorale americana.
 
Il cortocircuito, i 20 secondi diventati celebri, quando Trump cioè interviene e parla di Terza guerra mondiale, accade qui e sono convinto sia avvenuto per il clima instaurato e per una ulteriore incomprensione linguistica. 

A proposito della guerra Zelensky dice: “durante una guerra tutti hanno problemi… anche voi ne avrete, ma avete un bell’Oceano…” 
Trump (lo interrompe): “non ci dire cosa avremo e cosa sentiremo, non sei nella posizione di saperlo”.

Da adesso in poi sapete già tutto. Zelensky prova a dire che non intendeva dire che l’America avrà problemi, ma che sentiranno anche loro l’effetto della guerra. 
Non importa. Alle orecchie stanche di Trump e dei presenti è arrivata la frase spocchiosa di Zelensky che sta dicendo al mondo “avrete problemi anche voi”. 

Certamente Trump è un cafone. Certamente l’atteggiamento di superiorità di certi americani è insopportabile. 

Ma Zelensky è stato presuntuoso, semplicemente. O ingenuo. Entrambe due le cose sono preoccupanti. 

Sei a casa loro, sei in minoranza, tieni di fronte le telecamere di tutto il mondo, per quale motivo non capisci che è fondamentale che tu esprima tutto quello che vuoi con precisione nella tua lingua madre? Non vai all’incontro più importante della tua vita e della vita del tuo popolo senza avere la certezza di saper gestire il confronto. 

Chi oggi elogia Zelensky, dicendo che è stato bravissimo a non perdere il controllo davanti alle provocazioni di Trump, non sa di cosa parla. 

La mia opinione è che se Trump e Putin trovano un accordo, Zelensky ha finito di fare la star. Magari si è sentito così davanti ai media americani, mentre provava il suo show. 

Peccato che questo non fosse il Saturday Night Live.

The Founding Fathers vigorously debated the composition of the Senate, as much liberty was at stake. For example, if there were an “equality of suffrage,” each state, no matter how small it was, could be on equal footing with much larger states. This “equality” would REALLY represent “inequality” since today’s “red states,” with fewer voters, could produce a MAGA-majority in the Senate, which could (and would) dominate American politics. 
     If there were—on the other hand—an “inequality of suffrage,” then larger states, such as today’s California, would have many more Senators in Congress than just two. “Inequality” of this type (as to representation in the Senate) would ensure that larger “blue states” would NOT be dominated by smaller “red states.”
       Founding Father Luther Martin (AG from Maryland) reported the results from the Constitutional Convention debates: “On the votes being taken, Massachusetts, Pennsylvania, Virginia, North Carolina, and South Carolina, voted for the inequality. Connecticut, New York, New Jersey, Delaware, and Maryland were in the negative. Georgia had only two representatives on the floor, one of whom (not, I believe, because he was against the measure, but from a conviction, that we would go home, and thereby dissolve the convention, before we would give up the question,) voted also in the negative, by which that State was divided. Thus, Sir, on this great and important part of the system, the convention being equally divided, five States for the measure, five against, and one divided” (p. 188, Records of the Federal Convention).
      Clearly, we are suffering TODAY from the fatal errors of the Founding Fathers in granting smaller states MORE political leverage (i.e., more political power) than larger states (as to Senate representation). 
     The solution to this ‘MAGA-madness” (in the Senate) is secession. Blue states need to LEAVE this union and recreate themselves as new countries!

comments.author: @MariekePost
comments.text:
Look, we should respect the various perspectives on this issue. However, from an international law standpoint, Russia's invasion of Ukraine is a clear violation of the UN Charter, which prohibits the use of force against another country's sovereignty. It also breaches agreements like the Budapest Memorandum, in which Russia committed to respecting Ukraine's borders. Even when considering specific geopolitical justifications, claiming this act is anything other than aggression under international law is a misguided argument. It benefits no one to view it differently.

If Vance were even a fraction of the man he claims to be, he would travel to Ukraine to validate his stance. The idea that “I don’t need to have been there to know” is appalling. Many people still arguing that Zelensky should essentially accept "the deal" to save his people—similar to what some say Palestinians should do in Gaza—have lost touch with what it means to be human. They have forgotten the importance of pride, standing for something, and resisting the abuse of power. Many seem to mistakenly equate abuse of power with forcefulness these days, although, in fact, it is the most simplistic and destructive tactic to achieve one’s aims.

Trump is looking to fight… with everyone. Not just Zelensky. So why on earth should Zelensky succumb to anyone openly disrespecting him in the global arena?

And let’s be clear—I never said NATO’s conduct was indisputable. That’s why I started this whole conversation the way I did. But here’s what still doesn’t add up: If Putin truly saw NATO’s actions as an existential threat, why didn’t he address it more forcefully in the public domain first? He could have exposed NATO’s passive-aggressiveness and pushed for a serious debate. Instead, he gave no notice, changed his justifications multiple times, and invaded. If his true goal was protecting Russian-speaking people, why not exhaust diplomatic channels before throwing his own soldiers into the fire?

To me, it seems he just wanted to invade Ukraine and reclaim what he considers "Russian territory." He literally said as much. And that tells us something: He wasn't looking to solve a problem—he was looking to expand his reach.

So yes, we should be critical of both sides, because they both contributed to this mess, and we’re all suffering for it. But let’s not confuse complexity with false equivalence. Putin started the war on the wrong grounds. Period.

And this conversation was a disgrace. 

If it was a trap, it was devilish.

I respect and appreciate every US citizen who is not proud of what happened in the oval office on Friday. I'm not saying that an average American doesn't have the right to get frustrated by how much money is sent Ukraine's way with all the problems that the US is facing internally. My dear American friends,

Thank you for your unwavering words of support throughout all this time. If you can, please remind your politicians of everything Ukraine has done at their request:

🔹 1992 – As an independent Ukraine, we extended the treaty with the U.S. for the elimination of intermediate-range missiles.

🔹 1994 – We gave up nuclear weapons, including 130 missiles and 33 bombers with 1,700 nuclear warheads, under security guarantees signed by the U.S.

🔹 2003 – We participated alongside the U.S. in the Iraq War (18 of our soldiers died), which angered Saudi Arabia.

🔹 2010 – At the request of the U.S., we handed over all our highly enriched uranium, enough to create multiple nuclear warheads.

🔹 2020 – At the U.S.’s request, we blocked China from buying Motor Sich, enraging Beijing.

Now, russia is attacking us—the same russia to whom we once sent part of our own missiles. China, whom we defied at the U.S.’s request, is watching. And Saudi Arabia is discussing our fate with russia behind our backs.

We are deeply grateful for the assistance we have received from the U.S. over the years. But, if I’m being honest, I would rather have all those missiles and nuclear warheads right now than all the American military support.

I know that Americans would support helping Ukraine even if we had not agreed to all these requests from your government.

Maybe we are not the best at diplomacy or diplomatic restraint. Sorry. We are a young democracy and the poorest country in Europe. We are exhausted—emotionally and physically—from the loss of tens of thousands of people and hundreds of thousands of abducted children.

These losses would never have happened if we still had our nuclear weapons and missiles.

And right now, the whole world knows it.

Support your own security by supporting us. Otherwise, Ukraine’s story will become a cautionary tale, and the world will grow far more dangerous for everyone.

comments.text:
In the Presidents Trump and Zelensky press conference, JD Vance claims that war in the last three years did not bring peace, let’s try diplomacy. President Zelenskyy counters that Ukraine has tried diplomacy since 2014 and Putin broke every one of the 25 agreements. To this JD Vance grew angry for being corrected and started to attack Zelenskyy for his “disrespect” of the Oval Office, for his attacking the administration?? and goes on to accuse Zelenskyy of forcing conscripts to the front line (I think Vance confuses what Putin did with Zelenskyy). After Trump claims that Ukraine is completely demolished, Zelenskyy says Ukraine is building back fast, come and see. To which Vance accuses Zelenskyy of giving orchestrated propaganda tours.  Clearly, these are Russian propaganda points.
	The meeting was going well. There was even some playful banter between Trump and Zelenskyy when they disagreed with how much aid Europe gave compared to the USA.
	Then, the prejudiced JD Vance could not allow an otherwise pleasant media conference to showcase Zelenskyy as a nice guy, raised his voice and accused Zelenskyy of the above mentioned points.  He was the one that was being disrespectful of a guest invited to the White House to explain his view.  It was shameful behavior on the part of JD Vance and he owes President Zelenskyy an apology.
	Unfortunately Trump took on his VP’s demeanor and with an angry red face, accused Zelenskyy of having a “bad attitude,” having a weak hand as in cards, and maybe starting World War III.  Trump says to Zelenskyy “make a deal or you have no country.” This statement implies that Putin will completely conquer and destroy Ukraine if USA does not help.  Maybe. Study shows that if Putin goes against Europe, he will lose.  {Putin’s economy will not sustain it). Yes, Europe is committed for the long term, as some European leaders have said. If Putin can win this war, why has he not already? His military is being decimated and demolished.  See the Youtube videos for yourself.  After the initial land grab of the annexed regions, Putin has not gain any significant amount of territory. In addition, they have lost territory in the Kursk area. 
	To those who claim that Ukraine will ultimately lose anyway, so why bother supporting a lost cause.  To pre-determine that Ukraine will lose is to not know history. At every step of the Revolutionary war, the rag-tag soldiers of the 13 colonies were outnumbered and “losing.”  If we had thrown in the towel, we would not have the USA. Also, do we not take into account moral principles and God?  On moral principle, we cannot allow a murderer, a war criminal, Putin, off the hook.  If we do, then it is a mockery of justice and God.  God works through people, but if good people don’t fight  and defeat evil, then evil triumphs and God is falsely accused of being impotent.
	President Zelenskyy wants security guarantees to go with the mineral deal.  Trump minimizes the concern by claiming that security is only 2% of the problem. Trump thinks that just having American workers there in Ukraine is in itself a guarantee because he really believes that Putin would show Trump respect and would not dare attack.  Meanwhile, while the two heads of state is talking, Putin is firing missiles into Ukraine.  No respect.
	I believe President Trump may be more negotiable and compassionate, but he is surrounded by hardliners, and bad advisors like JD Vance, who is an amateur and has no experience in foreign affairs. He comes off arrogant and brash.  No finesse or diplomacy.  Also Vance knowledge is limited, especially when it comes to Ukraine’s situation.

Hello,

Ton analyse est en partie vraie, je dirais, car qui a soutenu militairement et financièrement l’Ukraine ? C’est bien les États-Unis, sinon Zelensky aurait capitulé direct. Après, tout le monde le sait, les US, faut pas leur faire confiance. Déjà en 39-45, ils sont arrivés quand ça sentait le cramé, après la bataille, alors que les Russes se battaient comme des lions, notamment à Stalingrad, la ville du patron de l’époque ! Sans le front russe, pas sûr que le débarquement américain aurait fonctionné. À la fin de la guerre, les US détenaient 50 % du stock d’or mondial, c’était pas gratuit leur débarquement… Là, c’est pareil, intérêt perso, oubliez pas, c’est America First ! Donc Zelensky ne comprend pas pourquoi les US l’ont soutenu pour le lâcher après 3 ans de combat et des milliers de soldats morts pour… rien ? C’est de là que vient sa frustration, et bon, y’a de quoi… Tous ces morts pour ça ? Pour dire stop comme ça ?

La réalité du terrain, Zelensky la connaît déjà : c’est que la Russie se rapproche trop de la Chine, et ça, c’est dangereux pour les US. C’est pas une histoire de soutien à l’Ukraine, limite Zelensky est un pion vu des US, mais ça, il le savait déjà aussi. Donc jouer les durs à la Maison Blanche ne changera rien malheureusement, car l’Europe n’a ni l’envie ni les moyens financiers d’aider.

Et bon, les 2000 ont décidé de siffler la fin de la récré, donc on joue plus, point. Macron est plus intelligent de ce point de vue : il sait qu’il ne peut pas bouger les USA facilement, donc il n’insiste pas trop. La guerre est plus large que l’Ukraine, c’est une guerre USA vs Chine, et la Russie peut faire basculer la game en faveur de l’un ou l’autre. comments.text:
Votre analyse met en lumière plusieurs aspects fondamentaux du conflit en Ukraine, notamment les jeux de pouvoir entre grandes nations, la pression écrasante sur Volodymyr Zelensky et les implications humaines dramatiques. 

Le conflit en Ukraine dépasse de loin une simple opposition militaire ; il s’inscrit dans une dynamique géopolitique où chaque acteur poursuit ses propres intérêts stratégiques. Les États-Unis, souvent perçus comme des alliés, n'agissent jamais sans calcul. Loin d'être un simple bénéficiaire d'une aide désintéressée, Zelensky se retrouve pris entre deux forces titanesques : la Russie, avec son impératif impérial, et les États-Unis, dont les soutiens sont toujours conditionnés par des intérêts cachés.

Sa frustration est probablement d’un homme qui porte sur ses épaules le destin d’un pays ravagé par la guerre, devant composer avec des pressions multiples tout en gérant l’effusion quotidienne de sang. Chaque jour, des milliers de vies sont brisées, rendant toute approche simpliste du conflit réductrice. Comparer cette situation à une simple ingratitude ordinaire revient à minimiser l’ampleur du drame humain en jeu. 

On peut aussi souligné  l’arrogance dans l’attitude de Trump, qui donne souvent l’impression de se placer au-dessus des autres, que ce soit sur la scène nationale ou internationale. Son style de leadership repose sur une posture de domination, une certitude absolue en ses décisions et un mépris affiché pour ses opposants. 


L’histoire jugera si cette guerre, au-delà des discours et des stratégies, aura réellement été menée pour la liberté d’un peuple ou pour servir des intérêts plus vastes et moins avouables.

Il y'a des choses a retenu dans l'analyse et il n'est probablement pas adaptée a l'empleur de la situation 

Peace en love

Excuse-moi, mon frère, avec tout mon respect pour toi… Une remarque sur ton idée : tes propos sur l'ingratitude sont justes dans d'autres contextes, mais en ce qui concerne ce qui s'est passé à la Maison-Blanche entre les deux présidents, ils ne sont pas exacts… et même contradictoires. La preuve en est ce qu’a déclaré le vice-président J.D. Vance. Il a dit à Zelensky – et je traduis de l’anglais : « Assez de confrontation frontale avec Poutine, il est maintenant temps pour la diplomatie. »

Zelensky lui a alors répondu : « Que voulez-vous dire par diplomatie ? Nous avons essayé toutes les formes de diplomatie avec Poutine depuis 2014, etc. »

Tu affirmes que Trump voulait trancher la question d’un coup de « couteau » définitif… Non, non ! La mentalité de Trump ne fonctionne pas ainsi. Il est spontané, il parle sans filtre, il est impulsif… enfin, il a un égo surdimensionné. Celui qui a déclenché l’étincelle, ce n’est pas lui, mais son vice-président ( mkawad fi rasso)… Il voulait se donner des airs de « Je suis le vice-président des États-Unis, pas comme les anciens depuis deux siècles ! » Il est entré en bourrin, cassant tout sur son passage, alors que Zelensky était venu seul, sans invitation officielle de l'administration américaine...
Son intention était de négocier et de signer un accord sur les métaux, mais les Américains ont fait preuve de bêtise… Ils n’ont même pas essayé de ménager un peu cet homme qui se bat depuis trois ans sans relâche contre la plus puissante armée du monde....
Non, ton raisonnement est erroné. Le contexte et ses données sont totalement différents. C'est l'Amérique qui est à l'origine du projet de guerre contre la Russie, et non Zelensky. Lui voulait faire passer un message – comme il l’a dit lui-même : « J’étais seul à me battre avec mes soldats, personne n’était avec moi. »...
Trump lui a alors répondu : « Tu n’étais pas seul, nous t’avons soutenu avec des armes et de l’argent. »...
Zelensky voulait faire comprendre que cette guerre n'était pas uniquement la sienne contre la Russie, mais bien celle des États-Unis en premier lieu, et de l’Europe aussi. Et il a raison : sans l’assurance du soutien de l’OTAN, Zelensky ne se serait jamais lancé dans cette guerre....les USA  ont trahi l'Europe et zelinski tout autant...il y a quelque chose cachée derrière tout cela, un accord entre USA et Poutine plus valeureux que l'accord des minéraux.. comments.text:
Analyse intéressante, mais je trouve que ton approche est un peu trop orientée en faveur de Trump. Certes, le principe psychologique de l'ingratitude que tu mets en avant est pertinent, et il y a une vraie réflexion sur la dépendance aux aides. Cependant, réduire cet affrontement à une simple question de psychologie individuelle me semble réducteur.

D'un côté, Trump ne fixe pas des limites uniquement par principe de gestion saine, mais aussi pour des raisons électorales et stratégiques. De l'autre, Zelensky ne réagit pas juste par ingratitude, mais parce que son pays est en guerre et qu'il cherche désespérément du soutien.

L’aide américaine à l’Ukraine n’est pas un simple "cadeau" : elle sert aussi les intérêts des États-Unis en freinant la Russie. Dans ce contexte, dire que Zelensky devrait "simplement dire merci" revient à ignorer les réalités géopolitiques.

Un peu plus de nuance aurait rendu ton analyse encore plus percutante. C’est dommage, car ton contenu est bien construit et pousse à la réflexion, mais ici, ça penche trop d’un côté. À voir si tu pourrais proposer une vision plus équilibrée dans une prochaine vidéo !

replies.author: @smic-cs4dl
replies.text:
@@HNaza Je ne suis pas d’accord. Je suis assez déçue par le manque de neutralité de TF1.

Lorsqu’on regarde la vidéo brute, sans commentaires, à froid et sans idées préconçues sur les protagonistes, on remarque que Trump souhaitait donner une conférence de presse assez classique, en restant en surface avec les journalistes, sans entrer dans les détails des discussions. C’est en réalité Zelensky qui a pris l’initiative d’aborder le fond du sujet, allant même jusqu’à préparer des photos pour illustrer son propos devant les journalistes. Trump, lui, le laisse faire.

La conversation commence alors à dégénérer. On voit bien que Trump cherche à écourter l’échange avec les journalistes. C’est pourquoi j’estime qu’on frôle la désinformation lorsque j’entends des journalistes affirmer que tout était orchestré par Trump. J’ai plutôt vu un Zelensky cherchant à profiter de l’attention médiatique pour pousser Trump à adopter une position plus offensive dans cette guerre, notamment lorsqu’il lui lance qu’il doit agir ainsi s’il veut être “le prochain Washington”.

Sur la forme, on assiste donc à une confrontation où chacun tente d’imposer son point de vue. Mais sur le fond, le véritable désaccord est clair : Zelensky veut poursuivre la guerre et refuse, pour l’instant, tout cessez-le-feu. Il cherche à obtenir un soutien américain afin de prendre l’avantage sur la Russie avant d’envisager des négociations. De son côté, Trump s’y oppose, estimant que les États-Unis ont déjà suffisamment dépensé dans ce conflit et qu’il ne veut pas engager davantage de ressources, d’autant plus en raison du coût humain qui ne ferait que s’alourdir.

C’est bien cela, le cœur du débat, et pourtant, aucun journaliste ne semble vouloir l’exposer clairement. Encore une fois, on se focalise sur la forme au lieu de s’intéresser au fond…

comments.text:
Je suis assez déçue par le manque de neutralité de TF1.

Lorsqu’on regarde la vidéo brute, sans commentaires, à froid et sans idées préconçues sur les protagonistes, on remarque que Trump souhaitait donner une conférence de presse assez classique, en restant en surface avec les journalistes, sans entrer dans les détails des discussions. C’est en réalité Zelensky qui a pris l’initiative d’aborder le fond du sujet, allant même jusqu’à préparer des photos pour illustrer son propos devant les journalistes. Trump, lui, le laisse faire.

La conversation commence alors à dégénérer. On voit bien que Trump cherche à écourter l’échange avec les journalistes. C’est pourquoi j’estime qu’on frôle la désinformation lorsque j’entends des journalistes affirmer que tout était orchestré par Trump. J’ai plutôt vu un Zelensky cherchant à profiter de l’attention médiatique pour pousser Trump à adopter une position plus offensive dans cette guerre, notamment lorsqu’il lui lance qu’il doit agir ainsi s’il veut être “le prochain Washington”.

Sur la forme, on assiste donc à une confrontation où chacun tente d’imposer son point de vue. Mais sur le fond, le véritable désaccord est clair : Zelensky veut poursuivre la guerre et refuse, pour l’instant, tout cessez-le-feu. Il cherche à obtenir un soutien américain afin de prendre l’avantage sur la Russie avant d’envisager des négociations. De son côté, Trump s’y oppose, estimant que les États-Unis ont déjà suffisamment dépensé dans ce conflit et qu’il ne veut pas engager davantage de ressources, d’autant plus en raison du coût humain qui ne ferait que s’alourdir.

C’est bien cela, le cœur du débat, et pourtant, aucun journaliste ne semble vouloir l’exposer clairement. Encore une fois, on se focalise sur la forme au lieu de s’intéresser au fond…

comments.author: @Quenelle-750
comments.text:
Ah, TF1, toujours à la pointe du décryptage… enfin, façon de parler. Derrière cette mise en scène aux airs de grande révélation, il ne s’agit finalement que d’un énième exercice d’auto-persuasion pour éviter d’admettre l’évidence : Zelensky vient de subir un revers monumental, et les Américains commencent (enfin !) à comprendre que financer indéfiniment ce bourbier n’a plus aucun sens.

Pendant des mois, la propagande a vendu l’image d’un Occident uni, indéfectiblement attaché au soutien de l’Ukraine. Mais voilà que Trump, malgré tous ses défauts, rappelle un principe de base : les intérêts américains passent avant les lubies bellicistes d’un gouvernement ukrainien qui refuse toute négociation. Et là, patatras ! TF1 et consorts doivent réajuster leur narratif : "Oh, regardez, c’est une humiliation, une mise en scène !" Oui, bien sûr, et la guerre en Ukraine est une promenade de santé, tant qu’on ne parle pas des milliers de jeunes envoyés au massacre sur ordre de leurs dirigeants corrompus.

Mais ce qui est encore plus grotesque, c’est le silence absolu sur la responsabilité française dans cette tragédie. Où était le décryptage quand Macron envoyait des canons Caesar et des missiles SCALP pour alimenter cette guerre, tout en se pavanant comme "artisan de la paix" ? Où étaient ces grands médias quand la France se couchait devant Washington, acceptant de ruiner son économie au nom de sanctions qui n’ont fait qu’enrichir les États-Unis ?

Alors non, ce clash historique entre Trump et Zelensky ne changera rien à la réalité du terrain : des soldats ukrainiens continuent de mourir, non pas pour défendre leur pays, mais pour satisfaire l’orgueil d’un président qui préfère s’accrocher à son rôle de "héros de la démocratie" plutôt que de chercher un compromis. Mais continuez, TF1, continuez de décrypter le vide, pendant que le sang coule.

Questa non è un'opinione politica, solo un'osservazione.
Capisco perfettamente che molti possano avere opinioni negative su come è andata, ma quello che ho capito guardando è questo:

Zelensky potrebbe non voler far terminare il conflitto tramite un accordo gestito dagli USA.
E in realtà non è così assurdo.
Qualsiasi accordo raggiunto con la Russia sotto la "sponsorizzazione" degli USA finirà inevitabilmente con la perdita di una parte dell'Ucraina o con qualche altra perdita altrettanto pesante per il paese.
Zelensky potrebbe voler puntare su un sostegno prolungato da parte dell'UE se/quando gli USA si ritireranno completamente, per continuare a combattere contro la Russia con l'obiettivo, irraggiungibile, di vincere il conflitto.

Ora, questo è ciò che Zelensky POTREBBE volere, SE vogliamo dare credito a questa linea di ragionamento.

Perché se non è così, allora quello che ho imparato oggi è che Zelensky è un completo idiota, senza neanche un briciolo di comprensione di base sulle relazioni pubbliche e la diplomazia.
Quello che ho visto è che:

Durante un incontro trasmesso in diretta mondiale,
Mentre è responsabile dell'intero dannato paese,
Sotto un conflitto militare in una posizione di forte svantaggio,
Contro un nemico molto più forte, che non ha i mezzi per contrastare senza il supporto dei paesi vicini,
Si ritrova finalmente in una posizione in cui potrebbe mettere fine a tutto questo in un modo che non porti a una sconfitta totale e inevitabile, e cosa fa?

Insulta Putin, definendolo un terrorista in diretta televisiva, il che, vero o meno (e penso sia vero), è probabilmente la cosa più stupida che abbia mai visto nel contesto di una possibile soluzione pacifica.
Antagonizza il Presidente e il Vicepresidente degli USA, tirando fuori vecchi "errori" di 10 anni fa, metà dei quali nemmeno sotto la diretta influenza dell'attuale amministrazione, e tutto questo di nuovo, in diretta globale.
Ha detto che Putin ha infranto accordi precedenti, e non ho dettagli o conoscenze al riguardo, ma diciamo per ipotesi che sia vero: e allora? Che cosa può fare al riguardo?
Assolutamente nulla, se non, da idiota qual è, scavarsi ancora di più la fossa sua e del suo paese, visto che non esiste alcuno scenario in cui possa uscire vincitore da questa situazione palesemente disastrosa.

Mi viene in mente il detto "trovarsi tra l'incudine e il martello", solo che in questo caso sta prendendo a pugni l'incudine sperando di romperla, mentre l'unica cosa che si sta rompendo è la sua mano

Tu demanderais à un boulanger son avis sur la mécanique d’un avion ? Ce n’est pas le monde des Bisounours où tout le monde peut voter sur des questions aussi complexes que la géopolitique et la guerre. Ces décisions nécessitent des années d’analyse, des données stratégiques que le grand public n’a pas, et une compréhension profonde des enjeux militaires, économiques et diplomatiques.

Croire qu’un référendum sur un conflit international serait pertinent, c’est se bercer d’illusions. La réalité, c’est que ces sujets dépassent largement le simple avis populaire. Vouloir simplifier une guerre à un ‘pour ou contre’ montre justement une méconnaissance totale du sujet.

Bei mir sind noch folgende Fragen offen: 
Warum möchten so viele jetzt sehen, wie der Sozialstaat in Deutschland zusammengestrichen wird und alle jungen Menschen in die Bundeswehr zwingen? Warum denken diese Leute, dass das nun der einzige Weg ist, den wir in Deutschland gehen können und warum scheinen sie sich darüber zu freuen? 
Der „Sozialstaat“ ist ja eine Versicherung, in die wir alle einzahlen und wir sollten doch in unserem eigenen Sinne gute Versicherungspolicen wählen bzw. dafür protestieren. 

Warum erhalten andere Möglichkeiten weniger Beifall? Andere Möglichkeiten wären zum Beispiel Streichung von anderen Haushaltsposten, zum Beispiel von Subventionen oder die Lockerung der Schuldenbremse. 
Außerdem der entschlossenen Aufbau einer europäischen Profi-Armee.

replies.author: @TheIldebrandoz
replies.text:
La stampa italiana è fallita già da tempo, non tanto economicamente, ma eticamente e professionalmente. Sopravvive solo grazie ai finanziamenti pubblici, ai fondi d’investimento e agli interessi di gruppi di potere che la tengono in vita per manipolare l’opinione pubblica. Se dovessero basarsi esclusivamente sulla qualità e sulla domanda reale del mercato, farebbero la fame.
I giornalisti non sono più cani da guardia del potere, ma fedeli esecutori della propaganda imposta dall’alto. Non fanno più inchieste scomode, non danno voce ai cittadini, ma si limitano a rilanciare comunicati e narrative di comodo, censurando qualsiasi voce fuori dal coro. Il risultato è un’informazione omologata, priva di credibilità e completamente asservita a chi stacca gli assegni.
Nel frattempo, il pubblico si allontana sempre più dai media tradizionali, preferendo cercare fonti alternative, indipendenti o internazionali. La stampa mainstream, anziché interrogarsi sulle cause di questa crisi, risponde con la criminalizzazione del dissenso, etichettando chiunque osi mettere in discussione la narrativa ufficiale come ‘disinformazione’.
Ma il giochino sta per finire.... il pubblico si è accorto della truffa e, senza più lettori né fiducia, il sistema mediatico mainstream è destinato a implodere sotto il peso della sua stessa menzogna...tempo al tempo.

Una risposta ai tanti commenti che chiedono re-elezioni ucraine:
Il blocco elettorale è una prassi comune in tempi di guerra ed è esplicitamente previsto dalla Costituzione ucraina.

Questo fenomeno non è limitato all'Ucraina: durante la Seconda Guerra Mondiale, il Regno Unito posticipò le elezioni fino alla fine del conflitto, mentre la Germania adottò una misura analoga durante la Prima Guerra Mondiale. Anche la Francia rinviò le elezioni legislative del 1915, che si tennero solo nel 1919, al termine della guerra.

Inoltre, circa il 60% della popolazione ucraina continua a sostenere il presidente Zelensky, rendendo non necessaria una riorganizzazione del processo elettorale in questo contesto.

I'm not sure it can be said any more plainly than Zelensky has already said it, but I'll try.  Creating "peace" by allowing Russia to get away with occupying another country, allowing them to hold onto occupied territory after the cease fire, and not providing a guarantee of security to the rest of the occupied country against future Russian aggression is *not* a good peace negotiation.  It sets a very bad precedent and shows that the West won't stand up to acts of aggression, but is so selfish and so focused on their own comfort that they will sacrifice any people or territory that they see as unimportant just to avoid the hassle of a conflict.

What's even worse is that Trump has taken it a step beyond callous indifference and is now actively trying to exploit the situation to rob Ukraine.  We invested in helping Ukraine hold out against the invasion because it is in *our interest* to make the conflict as much of a disaster for Russia as possible to discourage future Russian aggression (not to mention the invaluable intel we have gotten on Russian capabilities and tactics against Western hardware).  Now to suggest that not only should their leader grovel before us and offer his thanks but also repay the investments we made in *our own* interests... If this is really how Americans think we should treat other nations of the world, then eventually we'll pay the price.  There is no "manifest destiny" that is ours, there is no higher power that will ensure our success.  That kind of arrogant and corrupt behavior will be our downfall, as it has seen the downfall of every empire in history that has trod a similar path.

comments.text: C'est assez basique en fait, l'affaire avait été préparée d'avance comme un "win-win" en faveur du clan des MAGA:  soit le président élu de l'Ukraine venait par delà l'océan pour livrer une offrande en cadeau aux pieds du "roi" (du superlatif...) avant de lui baiser l'anneau, soit il repartait après avoir été instrumentalisé dans cette parodie qui ne trompe personne à moins d'être déjà profondément endoctriné.  Or sur le long terme ce gain médiatique apparent ne passera pas le test du temps et tout bon stratège d'expérience sait d'ailleurs que la victoire comporte parfois son lot de défaites éphémères.  Des enregistrements vidéo fort éloquents d'une valeur Historique viennent d'alimenter une mémoire collective qui n'est pas à la veille d'oublier ce spectacle on ne peut plus dérisoire, conçu visiblement pour justifier une suite d'actions semblables aux précédentes à n'en pas douter!  Par exemple blâmer le juste représentant d'un pays brutalement envahi après avoir abdiqué dans un passé pas si lointain comme puissance nucléaire à la demande des 2 mêmes super-puissances impliquées, lesquelles ont renié chacune à sa façon la parole donnée, prétendant défendre la paix tout comme lors de cette "crise" pré-programmée.  Alors, gloire à l'Ukraine et aux braves qui défendent son peuple!!

Let me briefly tell you an amazing story... Nuclear weapons were taken away and a memorandum was signed — the Budapest Memorandum, signed on December 5, 1994, by Ukraine, the United States, the United Kingdom, and Russia (later joined by China and France as well). The memorandum provided security assurances to Ukraine in exchange for its renunciation of nuclear weapons. Ukraine agreed to give up its nuclear arsenal inherited from the Soviet Union, and in return, the signatory countries pledged to respect Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity.

However, after 2014, Russia invades and takes Crimea and parts of Donbas. Then, in February 2022, Russia launches a full-scale invasion of all of Ukraine. Do you know the reasons for the invasion as stated by both Putin and the Russian Foreign Ministry? The reason is: Ukraine chose a pro-Western path, Ukraine is friends with the United States, and Ukraine wants to join NATO.

The war has been ongoing for 3 years. People are dying on both sides—Russian occupiers and Ukrainian defenders. Russia bombs civilian buildings, and even an oncology hospital for children was bombed (there's plenty of evidence online). In general, the conditions of the agreement are not being fulfilled by either the UK or the US... weapons are barely being provided. Inside their own countries, there are kickbacks, cuts, and other corruption schemes, including in your own US (even Elon Musk confirmed this). Ultimately, the new US president claims that Ukraine is to blame for Russia's invasion and that it wouldn't have happened under his leadership (but what difference does it make what would have happened under him? I saw the complete press conference video. Here's my take,
1) Zelensky actually had the deal. Trump agreed that US support would continue after the signing of the deal. Trump also assured that security guarantees will also be given once the deal is signed and a ceasefire is done. 
2) Zelensky had to endure trump and vance only for a few more minutes. But he became confrontational at the last 15 minutes.
3) He picked up fight with Vance, who was blaming biden, but zelensky got offended and asked "what kind of diplomacy do you mean". Up untill that point everyone was looking at and answering to the media but zelensky asked this to Vance directly eye to eye. 
4) And then his statement, "you are fine because of the oceans but someday you will feel" was the final nail in the coffin. That statement offended trump very much. 
5) Trump then nuked zelensky and the deal and everything broke down. 
Moral of the story :- Don't be confrontational to the person whose support you need the most at the time. Even china NEVER confronted US when they were a growing, developing country. All this aggresion from china only came after 2015, 2016, when they thought that they were powerful enough to not be passive. 
We MUST do the same. We also must NOT be confrontational to US because a huge part of our growth depends on US. We can be confrontational with anyone except US for now. Once we become powerful enough, we no longer need to be passive.

comments.text:
I usually agree with PD sir's analysis, but NOT THIS ONE.

Zelensky was NOT  being ULTRA AGGRESSIVE. And anyone who saw the full debate will know this.

 Zelensky was not given the respect he deserves as a President. It was more of a bullying tactic by Trump and JD Vance to corner Zelensky into yielding before US demands.

To add to the disrespect, a white houe journalist asked Zelensky whether he even had suits, since he is not wearing one.

Also, not wearing a suit to oval office is disrespect now? Already knowing he has given up on wearing this, as a mark of solidarity for his fellow citizens fighting the war.

Also, a president commenting sarcastically on the attire of a fellow President, THAT is Disrespect. 

WHY SHOULD ANYONE TOLERATE THIS HUMILIATION, LET ALONE A PRESIDENT OF A VISITING NATION STATE?

The US aid was supposed to be a grant. Now retrospectively they want to turn it into a debt to extract and pressurise Ukraine into yielding its resources. 

It is like the next finance minister, asking citizens to pay income tax for salary above 7 lakhs (for the previous year), making a stupid argument that it was not me who brought this income tax relief in the first place.

Zelensky stood composed for majority of the discussion, understanding what is at stake. But he had to draw a line somewhere, just like any self respecting individual.

This analysis reminds me of the phrase, "The story will always be written from the perspective of the hunter, until the lion learns how to hunt"

He expresses his hypocrisy very well. Marco Rubio, prior to Donald Trump’s election in November 2024, was a steadfast supporter of Ukraine, a fierce critic of Russia, and a vocal champion of President Volodymyr Zelensky. As a senior U.S. senator and a member of the Senate Intelligence and Foreign Relations Committees, Rubio consistently advocated for strong American backing of Ukraine in its fight against Russian aggression.

From the earliest days of Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022, Rubio was among the loudest voices in Washington calling for decisive action. He warned about the invasion before it happened and later supported bipartisan measures to send military aid to Ukraine. In March 2022, he declared that “Putin’s war is an attack on democracy itself,” emphasizing that Ukraine’s resistance was vital not just for its survival but for global stability. Throughout 2022 and 2023, Rubio backed sanctions against Russia, military assistance for Ukraine, and efforts to hold the Kremlin accountable for war crimes.

Rubio also praised President Zelensky’s leadership on multiple occasions. In a June 2023 Senate hearing, he lauded Zelensky for advancing democratic reforms and standing firm against Russian aggression. In a September 2024 interview, he called Zelensky a “pivotal leader in Eastern Europe.” His unwavering support for Ukraine, his denunciation of Putin’s brutality, and his vocal admiration for Zelensky all underscore that, prior to Trump’s election, Marco Rubio was one of the Senate’s most outspoken advocates for Ukraine’s fight for sovereignty and freedom.

comments.author: @lethanh4480
comments.text:
Trong suốt cuộc kháng chiến chống Mỹ, Việt Nam nhận được sự hỗ trợ lớn từ các nước xã hội chủ nghĩa, đặc biệt là Liên Xô và Trung Quốc. Tuy nhiên, điều đó không đồng nghĩa với việc họ hoàn toàn ủng hộ Việt Nam thống nhất. Mỗi quốc gia đều có lợi ích riêng, và sự thống nhất của Việt Nam không phải lúc nào cũng phù hợp với chiến lược của họ.

Trung Quốc, dù viện trợ rất nhiều cho Việt Nam, nhưng họ cũng có những toan tính riêng. Trung Quốc không muốn Việt Nam trở nên quá mạnh, vì điều đó có thể ảnh hưởng đến vị thế của họ ở Đông Nam Á. Hơn nữa, một Việt Nam thống nhất và hùng mạnh có thể gây lo ngại cho Trung Quốc, đặc biệt là khi Việt Nam có quan hệ chặt chẽ với Liên Xô – đối thủ của Trung Quốc trong phong trào cộng sản quốc tế. Vì vậy, Trung Quốc vừa hỗ trợ Việt Nam chống Mỹ, nhưng cũng giới hạn sự hỗ trợ ở mức độ nhất định, thậm chí sau này còn có xung đột trực tiếp với Việt Nam vào năm 1979.

Mỹ, với chính sách kiềm chế chủ nghĩa cộng sản, dĩ nhiên không muốn Việt Nam thống nhất dưới chế độ cộng sản. Ngay từ đầu, Mỹ đã can thiệp để duy trì một chính quyền thân Mỹ ở miền Nam. Sau khi thất bại trong chiến tranh, Mỹ tiếp tục áp đặt cấm vận, cô lập Việt Nam nhằm ngăn cản sự phát triển của một quốc gia thống nhất do Đảng Cộng sản lãnh đạo. Dù sau này quan hệ Việt - Mỹ cải thiện, nhưng trong giai đoạn chiến tranh, Mỹ luôn tìm cách duy trì sự chia cắt.

Liên Xô, dù là đồng minh quan trọng của Việt Nam, cũng không hẳn muốn Việt Nam thống nhất quá nhanh. Đối với Liên Xô, Việt Nam là một quân bài quan trọng trong cuộc đối đầu với Mỹ, nhưng việc thống nhất quá sớm có thể làm thay đổi cán cân chiến lược trong khu vực. Hơn nữa, sự thống nhất của Việt Nam có thể kéo theo những vấn đề phức tạp, đặc biệt là trong quan hệ giữa Việt Nam và Trung Quốc – hai nước mà Liên Xô đều muốn tranh thủ.

Tuy nhiên, Việt Nam đã khôn khéo tận dụng sự ủng hộ của các nước lớn để phục vụ lợi ích của mình. Năm 1972, khi Trung Quốc bắt tay với Mỹ để thoát khỏi tình trạng cô lập và đổi lấy sự công nhận tại Liên Hợp Quốc, viện trợ cho Việt Nam bắt đầu giảm sút. Liên Xô, khi thấy Mỹ và Trung Quốc xích lại gần nhau, cũng phải tìm cách giảm căng thẳng với Mỹ, khiến viện trợ dành cho Việt Nam không còn dồi dào như trước. Về phía Mỹ, khi đã đạt được thỏa thuận với Trung Quốc, Washington cũng giảm viện trợ cho Việt Nam Cộng Hòa vì nhận thấy Trung Quốc là một đối tác quan trọng hơn.

Trước bối cảnh đó, Việt Nam Dân chủ Cộng hòa đã tận dụng tối đa khoảng thời gian còn nhận được viện trợ để củng cố lực lượng, tích lũy đủ sức mạnh cho cuộc tổng tiến công năm 1975. Khi các nước lớn vẫn còn đang điều chỉnh chiến lược của mình, Việt Nam đã hành động quyết đoán, tiến hành chiến dịch quân sự tổng lực và giành chiến thắng trước sự ngỡ ngàng của chính những cường quốc từng can thiệp vào chiến tranh Việt Nam.

Như vậy, dù nhận được nhiều sự giúp đỡ từ các cường quốc, Việt Nam vẫn phải tự mình quyết định vận mệnh dân tộc. Không một quốc gia nào thực sự mong muốn Việt Nam thống nhất một cách mạnh mẽ, ngoại trừ chính người Việt Nam. Điều đó càng làm nổi bật tinh thần độc lập, tự chủ và ý chí kiên cường của dân tộc trong hành trình giành lại hòa bình và thống nhất đất nước.

Bài học từ Việt Nam cho thấy, một quốc gia nhỏ muốn sinh tồn và phát triển phải biết tận dụng thế cuộc, cân bằng giữa các cường quốc để bảo vệ lợi ích của mình. Điều này đặc biệt có ý nghĩa khi so sánh với tình hình Ukraine ngày nay. Khi chính quyền Trump lên nắm quyền, chính sách Mỹ đã thay đổi 180 độ so với Biden, bắt tay với Nga, ép Ukraine phải thỏa hiệp và đòi lại viện trợ trước đó bằng việc khai thác tài nguyên đất hiếm. Điều này cho thấy Ukraine đã thất bại trong việc cân bằng giữa các nước lớn khi đứng ở vị trí giao thoa quyền lực giữa Đông và Tây. Sự thay đổi trong chính sách của các cường quốc khiến Ukraine rơi vào thế bị động, không thể tận dụng sự ủng hộ để xoay chuyển tình thế như Việt Nam đã từng làm trong quá khứ.

Nghệ thuật kết thúc chiến tranh của Việt Nam là bài học lớn cho Ukraine. Việt Nam sẽ rất khó có được độc lập nếu không khôn khéo, bởi nếu đua sức bền, dù có thắng thì cũng kiệt quệ. Lịch sử Việt Nam đã nhiều lần chứng minh sự linh hoạt trong ngoại giao và quân sự. Nhà Lý từng chủ động tấn công Tống khi phát hiện ý đồ xâm lược, phá hủy kho tàng, đưa chiến tranh sang đất địch rồi tại trận Như Nguyệt, dù thắng lớn, Đại Việt vẫn chủ động đề nghị giảng hòa để nhà Tống không mất mặt. Trong cuộc chiến với Mông - Nguyên, dù ba lần chiến thắng, Đại Việt vẫn chấp nhận làm chư hầu, nhường danh nghĩa thiên mệnh cho nhà Nguyên để tránh binh đao lâu dài. Thời nhà Minh, khi đánh bại quân Minh, Lê Thái Tổ vẫn chấp nhận cho quân Minh giảng hòa tại Đông Quan, lập hội thề rút lui trong danh dự để tránh trả thù. Quang Trung Hoàng đế, dù đại thắng quân Thanh, vẫn nhanh chóng đưa sứ bộ sang xin thông hiếu, tránh tạo cớ để nhà Thanh phát động chiến tranh lần nữa.

Ngay cả trong thời hiện đại, năm 1979, khi Trung Quốc xâm lược Việt Nam và chịu thiệt hại nặng nề, Việt Nam có thể tiếp tục gây tổn thất lớn hơn nữa khi đã tổng động viên và có sự hỗ trợ của Liên Xô. Tuy nhiên, để tránh căng thẳng kéo dài, Việt Nam không đẩy mạnh truy kích mà chủ động để Trung Quốc rút quân trong danh dự. Điều đó giúp Việt Nam tránh một cuộc chiến hao tổn kéo dài và giữ vững sự ổn định chiến lược.

Những bài học này cho thấy rằng một quốc gia nhỏ muốn tồn tại phải biết khi nào chiến đấu, khi nào hòa hoãn và khi nào cần nhượng bộ có lợi. Nếu Ukraine không thể vận dụng những bài học này, họ sẽ tiếp tục lâm vào thế bị động trước các cường quốc, không thể tìm ra một lối thoát chiến lược phù hợp.

comments.author: @leechrec
comments.text:
I watched the entire press conference with Zelensky. There was 40  minutes of discussion up to the argument. Most people saw at most the last ten minutes. The whole video gives the proper context.

When I first watched the argument without the proper context, I thought it was possible that Trump and Vance ambushed Zelensky or were even trying to humiliate him. That's not what happened. 

You had 40 minutes of calm conversation. Vance made a point that didn't attack Zelensky and wasn't even addressed to him, and Zelensky clearly started the argument.

In the first 40 minutes, Zelensky kept trying to go beyond what was negotiated in the deal. When Trump was asked a question, it was always "we'll see." Zelensky made blanket assertions that there would be no negotiating with Putin, and that Russia would pay for the war. When Trump said that it was a tragedy that people on both sides were dying, Zelensky interjected that the Russians were the invaders.

For his part, Trump made clear that the US would continue delivering military aid. All Zelensky had to do was remain calm for a few more minutes and they would've signed a deal.

The argument started when Trump pointed out that it would be hard to make a deal if you talk about Putin the way Zelensky does. Vance interjects to make the reasonable point that Biden called Putin names and that didn't get us anywhere.

The Zelensky/Trump dynamic was calm and stable. It was when Vance spoke that Zelensky started to interrogate him. Throughout the press conference to that point, everyone was making their arguments directly to the  audience. Zelensky decided to challenge Vance and ask him hostile questions. He went back to his point that Putin never sticks to ceasefires, once again implying that negotiations are pointless. Why on earth would you do this? Then came the fight we all saw.

Zelensky was minutes away from being home free, and he would have had the deal and new commitments from the Trump administration. The point Vance made was directed against Biden and the media, taking them to task for speaking in moralistic terms. This offended Zelensky, and that began the argument.

I've been a fan of Zelensky up to this point, but this showed so much incompetence, if not emotional instability, that I don't see how he recovers from this. The relationship with the administration is broken. Ukraine should probably go with new leadership at this point.

Edit: Upon further thought, it seems to me that a deal had already been in place ready to sign and they were there to simply discuss it and also have certain agreed upon talking points. Zelensky then tried to make additional demands while the cameras were rolling. This was the first mistake. It was further heightened when he suggested that diplomacy with Putin would not work anyway because Putin did not respect prior ceasefire agreements . He wanted to understand how the US would ensure that a new ceasefire with Putin would not be broken again, which is a valid concern. But these things are better discussed behind closed doors. It was a risk he took but was ill timed and inappropriate for the occasion. Trump probably wanted the deal signed first before entertaining any additional requests (whether in good faith or not), but Zelensky wanted to supersede this.

Dear Senators Scott and Moody,

My 36-year career in national security, serving in the Air Force, FBI, & Leidos, began with 5 years flying as a B-52 Navigator and Radar Navigator (bombardier). I flew 1535 hours in the B-52, and spent years planning bombing, mining, and Harpoon missions into Eastern Europe and the Baltic Sea in support of our NATO allies. I had friends die for this country.

Tomorrow I will be writing to Secretary of State Rubio, National Security Advisor Waltz, and to the Joint Chiefs of Staff, asking them to resign in protest to President Trump's horrifying performance today.

More disgusted in Trump and his cult than I have ever been,

Yet, despite being in the middle of a war and relying on U.S. aid, Zelensky stood his ground. He shut them down with confidence, responding to every provocation in a calm, collected manner. I’m all the way Team Zelensky on this one. This was an unscripted display of Trump and Vance’s true colors.

Et puis cette proximité malaisante avec le Président de la République française (sans compter les vidéos sur les RS ou l'on voit très bien la complicité, puis le gars est dans son avion quand même xD), dans la même lignée des St Cricq/Duhamel, version 2.0, qui a pour cœur de cible le jeune publique ne regardant très peu les JT de papa, pour éviter au maximum que ces jeunes là diversifient leurs sources d'info, avec divers médias plus ou mois indépendants (seuls les plus curieux "résistent"). Cela fait déjà bien longtemps que le journalisme grand publique a trahi sa raison d'être, c'est à dire au service du peuple et non l'organe de diffusion du narratif des élites politiques et économiques,  avec de plus en plus de zèle, très consensuel dans leurs interviews notamment, de vériatbles chiens de garde, comme des courtisans dans la cours !
